phuket.title: Phuket dishes to look for
phuket.text: Moo hong: pork belly braised with soy, garlic and lots of black pepper, eaten with rice. Mee Hokkien: thick yellow noodles fried with pork, seafood and greens in a dark gravy, often with an egg on top. Mee hoon and mee sua: thin rice noodles and fine wheat noodles, fried or in pork bone soup. Phuket dim sum: small steamed and fried plates for breakfast, eaten with chilli sauce, from about 05:30. Khanom jeen: fresh rice noodles with your choice of Southern curry and a table of free herbs and pickles. Gaeng poo: crab meat curry with betel leaves, poured over thin rice noodles. Gaeng som (gaeng leung): sour, hot orange fish curry with tamarind and turmeric, no coconut milk. O tao: taro, egg and small oysters fried together until soft and crisp. Loba: fried pork offal and tofu with a sweet chilli dip. O aew: clear fig-seed jelly with shaved ice, red syrup and red beans. A pong: thin coconut crepes cooked over charcoal. Roti: flat bread fried on a griddle, with curry for breakfast or with banana and condensed milk as a sweet. Khanom tom, ang ku and other Peranakan sweets: small rice flour cakes with coconut and palm sugar, sold at markets and dessert shops. Kopi: Phuket coffee, strong and sweet with condensed milk, served in old coffee shops (kopitiam).

phuket.title: How ordering and paying works
phuket.text: Thai meals are shared: order one dish per person plus rice, put everything in the middle and say 'khao suay' for plain rice. Ask for 'mai phet' (not spicy) or 'phet nit noi' (a little spicy); Southern curries are very hot by default. Shophouses and markets have no service charge and are often cash only; Thai QR (PromptPay) payment needs a Thai bank app, so bring small notes. Smarter restaurants and hotels write prices with '++', which means 10% service charge plus 7% VAT are added; tipping is not expected at local shops, and 20-100 THB or the coins left on the tray is a kind extra at sit-down places.

phuket.title: When places open
phuket.text: Phuket Town eats early: dim sum shops open 04:00-06:00 and finish by 11:00, roti and khanom jeen shops run about 06:30-13:00, and many famous noodle shophouses close by 15:00-17:00. Dinner places open 17:00-18:00, and only a few cook after 23:00 (Go Benz to 01:30, Ko Ang Seafood to 23:30, Local Canteen to midnight). Many family shops close one day a week, often Monday, Tuesday or Wednesday, and some close on Buddhist holy days, so check the day. Night markets: Sunday Walking Street on Sunday, Naka on Saturday and Sunday, Chillva Monday to Saturday.

phuket.title: Where the pork is
phuket.text: The Hokkien-Chinese shops of the Old Town cook a lot of pork: moo hong, crispy pork, pork satay, loba and pork lard in the noodles. Muslim shops serve no pork and often no alcohol: you can tell them by a green halal sign (ฮาลาล in Thai) and menus of beef, chicken and goat curry with roti. They are common around Krabi and on Koh Yao and Koh Lanta, so aim for the pork places in this guide there.

phuket.title: Seafood priced by weight
phuket.text: At seafood places fish, crab, lobster and mantis shrimp are often sold by the kilo or by 100 g, and the menu may only say 'market price'. Before they cook, ask the weight and the total price ('kilo la thao rai?'), watch them weigh it, and write the total down. Local places in Phuket Town, Laem Hin and Kathu charge much less than beach restaurants; a 2024 review of one local Phuket seafood restaurant listed fish at 500-600 THB a kilo. Check the bill for items you did not order.

phuket.title: Coffee in Thailand
phuket.text: Thailand grows its own coffee: arabica in the northern hills of Chiang Rai, Chiang Mai and Nan (Doi Chang and Doi Tung are the best known names), and robusta in the south, mostly around Chumphon, Surat Thani and Ranong. A Thai iced coffee is sweet by default, with sugar and condensed milk: say 'wan noi' (less sweet) or 'mai sai nam tan' (no sugar), or order an Americano or a pour-over in a specialty shop. In 2026 a specialty espresso drink costs about 80-130 THB and a pour-over or signature drink 100-180 THB; a sweet iced coffee from a street stall is about 40-60 THB.

phuket.title: Fast food in Thailand
phuket.text: KFC is the biggest chain (more than 700 outlets), followed by McDonald's, Burger King, Thailand's own The Pizza Company, Pizza Hut, Domino's, Subway and Texas Chicken; Shake Shack is in Bangkok only, and we found no Five Guys in Thailand. The Thai menus add rice bowls with spicy or kaprao chicken, McDonald's pork burgers (Samurai Pork Burger 109 THB), Hat Yai-style and tom yum fried chicken and pork congee at Burger King, and corn or pineapple pies. Most mall outlets keep mall hours (about 10:00-22:00); drive-thru branches and several Patong, Khao San and Sukhumvit outlets are open 24 hours.

phuket.title: Delivery, 7-Eleven and what a meal costs
phuket.text: Grab (GrabFood) and LINE MAN deliver from the chains and from most burger shops in this list; the chains also take orders on their own numbers: McDonald's 1711, KFC 1150, The Pizza Company 1112. At any hour, 7-Eleven heats a ham and cheese toastie for about 30-45 THB. In 2026 a chain meal costs about 150-250 THB (a Big Mac set was 220 THB in late 2024, and Numbeo puts a fast-food meal in Bangkok at about 250 THB in Oct 2026), while a burger at a craft burger shop costs 250-600 THB.

bangkok.title: Street food: when stalls cook and how to pay
bangkok.text: Old Bangkok eats in two shifts: pork-leg, congee and noodle shops cook from about 7:00 and many sell out or close by 13:00-15:00, while Yaowarat and Banglamphu stalls open from about 17:00 to midnight. Monday is the weakest day, because many street vendors and Yaowarat stalls take it off. Most stalls are cash only; many show a Thai QR code (PromptPay) that needs a Thai bank app, so carry small notes (20, 100 THB). At famous stalls you often pay or order before you sit, and the queue moves faster than it looks.

bangkok.title: Michelin street stalls: is the queue worth it
bangkok.text: The 2026 Michelin Guide cut many old Chinatown and Bang Rak stalls (Nai Ek, Ouan Pochana, Jok Prince, Prachak are no longer listed), but Thai diners still rate them highly on Wongnai. Bib Gourmand means good value, not a long queue: places such as Krua Apsorn, K. Panich or Kolun.h usually take 0-20 minutes. Jay Fai, the one-star stall, means 2-3 hours of waiting and about 1,500 THB for the crab omelette; most groups are happier at Thipsamai or Fai Ta Lu nearby. Go at opening time or mid-afternoon to avoid the worst queues.

bangkok.title: Fine dining: booking and dress
bangkok.text: Book the starred restaurants weeks ahead: Nusara has about 10 seats at one table and Potong about 28, so a table for 8 needs early contact and sometimes a full buyout. Most take bookings on their own site, by phone or LINE, and some ask for a deposit or card guarantee. Prices are shown before 10% service and 7% VAT, so add about 17%. Dress smart casual; at hotel restaurants such as Le Normandie avoid shorts, sandals and sleeveless shirts.

bangkok.title: Getting around for food
bangkok.text: The MRT Blue Line is the easiest way in: Wat Mangkon for Yaowarat, Hua Lamphong for Talat Noi and Si Morakot, Sam Yot for Pratu Phi, the Giant Swing and Phraeng Phuthon, and Sanam Chai for Wat Pho and Tha Tien. The Chao Phraya Express boat links Tha Chang, Tha Tien, Ratchawong (Chinatown), Si Phraya, Oriental and Sathorn pier (BTS Saphan Taksin), and small cross-river ferries go to Wang Lang and Wat Arun. For 8 people book two Grab cars or a large car; Chinatown traffic is slow after 17:00, so walk the last part.
